newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies up sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies up sharply.

text.p: Rolling of longs from December in deferreds and other spread action continued to infleunce CME hog futures which closed mixed while a bullish out-of-town report kept pork bellies sharply higher, traders said.

Some traders continued to roll long December live hog contracts into the February lean contract while strong cash markets provided underlying support. December becomes the spot position on Monday and longs are bringing positions into line with exchange rules.
However, the strong tone to cash markets pushed December up to near its old high at one time.

Demand for hogs has been better than expected this week and expectations of steady to higher cash markets after the holiday kept December supported and it came to within 0.050 cent of its contract high at one time. The market is also technically strong after Tuesday's rally from early losses, they added.
LIT division of First Options notably spread long February/short December. Rand Financials and LFG bought February early and touched off buy stops, pit sources said.
In hog options, E.D. & F. Man took December 58 calls and sold 56 calls, thought to be liquidation. December call offerings kept a lid on December futures early, sources said.

Pork belly futures remained strong and rallied late to session highs on further demand prompted by Tuesday's bullish CME out-of-town report and the strong technical signals. Only light profit taking was cited at times, traders said.
The out-of-town report showed movement of product into approved warehouses at a much slower than expected pace and total stocks moving to below year ago levels, they said.
CME reported a net in-movement of 838,000 lbs versus analyst estimates for 2.5 to 3.0 million lbs net in. Stocks now total 18.267 million lbs compared with 20.882 million lbs on hand a year ago.
"The (futures) market needs to go up to stimulate storing of bellies," one trader said.
Hogs closed 0.700 cent higher to 0.975 cent lower, with December up 0.175 at 59.225 cents per cwt. Pork bellies ended 2.225 to 1.275 higher, with February up 1.975 at 79.375 cents.
Both contracts closed at noon CST and will remain closed Thursday for U.S. Thanksgiving.
